By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States of 
America, in order to correct a typographical error, it is hereby ordered that the 
adjusted maximum scale of pay in the Section 4103 Schedule for Director of Nursing 
Service, as set forth in Schedule 3 of Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is 
amended by ehanging “ 2,611*” to read “ 52,611*” .

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The whole order is one self-executing typographical correction of Schedule 3 of EO 11941; the text sets no later effective date, so it was complete on signing, October 25, 1976. It states no "until" date or deadline. The change continued inside EO 11941 and ended with that parent when EO 12010 Sec. 4 superseded it; that parent supersession is the end of the consequence, not of this order's own spent command.

research_rationale:
EO 11943 (41 FR 47213, signed 1976-10-25) corrects a typographical entry in Schedule 3 of EO 11941: "2,611*" becomes "52,611*" for the Section 4103 Schedule, Director of Nursing Service. The command is self-executing and complete on signing, so the whole order (one clause) ended on 1976-10-25 by performance on issue. The surviving consequence, the corrected figure, lived inside EO 11941, which EO 12010 Sec. 4 superseded ("Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is superseded."). The Federal Register disposition note on this order's record reads "Superseded by: EO 12010, September 28, 1977"; EO 12010 names only EO 11941, so that note is read as recording the parent's supersession and is not treated as the end of this order's own command, which was already spent. The bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register disposition notes) show no other later instrument.
